report.source_notes: Imports & weight: UN Comtrade (Jordan=400, partner World, flow M, CIF USD), pulled 2026-10-09. Customs: WITS/TRAINS MFN simple average 2023. Freight: China->Aqaba 20GP USD 5,275, Jul 2026 (Goodhope Freight); payload 18,800 kg = 80 aseptic drums x 235 kg per 20ft (tomatopaste.webnode.cn). China is the #2 supplier; Egypt (#1) is closer, so this is an upper bound. shipping_pct = (freight/payload)/import_price_per_kg_usd; CIF price already includes freight - do not add on top. Raw material: Ministry of Agriculture bulletin, Amman Central Market, 29 Mar 2026: tomatoes 30/40/50 piasters per kg; used 40 piasters = 0.40 JOD/kg. Ratio = paste Brix / fresh Brix = 29 / 4.5 (paste traded at 28-30 Bx, fresh tomatoes 3.5-5.5 Bx; Tridge tomato paste supply-chain note) = 6.4. Conversion cost (labour, energy, overheads) is an estimate. Raw-material availability evidence: Jordan is a large fresh-tomato exporter (WITS 070200 exports 2023: USD 107.2M, 52,020 t). Machinery cost: see machine_source. FX: 1 JOD = 1.4104 USD (CBJ peg 0.709).
report.machine_source: Made-in-China supplier listings, Oct 2026: Small tomato paste line USD 50,000 (methena) to high-concentrate line USD 490,000-500,000 (sinojump)

explanation.summary: Tomato paste scored 3.9 out of 10, so local manufacturing does not look attractive right now. The verdict was limited because producing locally (4.01 USD/kg) costs more than importing (1.44 USD/kg including customs).
reasons_for: Imports are sizeable: about 21.5 million USD in 2024, changing by 12.5% per year.
Local capability is reasonable: machinery 2/5, raw materials 5/5, skills 3/5.
The score is built from four transparent factors you can test in the what-if tool.
concerns: بنحتاج حوالي 6 كيلو بندورة لكيلو معجون، فكلفة الإنتاج المحلي أعلى بكثير من المستورد؛ بيع البندورة طازجة (تصدير 2.06$/كغ) بيجيب أكثر؛ الموردين قريبين والحماية قليلة

High capital requirement: the equipment alone is listed at 50,000 to 500,000 USD, and this is only part of the investment (ex-works supplier listing prices, excluding shipping, customs, installation, moulds and buildings).
The estimated local cost (4.01 USD/kg) leaves little advantage against an import cost of 1.44 USD/kg including customs (freight is already in the import price).
next_steps: Get written quotes from machinery and raw-material suppliers.
Talk to local wholesalers and retailers to confirm demand and target prices.
Check licensing, standards and incentives with the Jordan Investment Commission and the Chamber of Industry.
caveats: The figures for these items are estimates, not measured values: local production cost, conversion_cost_per_kg_usd, machinery availability, skills availability, number of local factories, market saturation level.
This is a quick screening estimate, not a business plan or financial advice.
